headline: COPPER COMEX ALL-TIME RECORD: $14,781/T AS 200K TONS FLOOD US PORTS IN JULY — Tariff-Driven Hoarding Meets Shrinking Ex-US Supply
snippet: Copper for September delivery touched $6.7045 per pound ($14,781 per tonne) on the COMEX on August 5, 2026, surpassing the prior intraday record set in mid-May and marking a fresh all-time high as tariff-driven hoarding pulled more than 200,000 tonnes of copper into US ports in July alone — the largest monthly inflow in over a decade. Prices are being driven by a dual dynamic: the US tariff framework finalised June 30 temporarily exempted refined copper imports, incentivising maximum front-running before phased tariffs begin in 2027, while the supply picture outside the United States continues to deteriorate from a combination of mine underperformance, China's sulphuric acid export restrictions (a critical copper smelting input), and COMEX inventory drawdowns. Goldman Sachs estimates copper may breach $14,000/t in nominal terms once tariffs take effect and the pre-tariff stockpile surge reverses. For junior copper developer valuations — which are still modelled at pre-tariff price assumptions in most sell-side models — a sustained copper price at $14,000+ would require material upward revisions to NAV estimates across the TSX-V and ASX developer space.

headline: GDX SURGES 8% TO 52-WEEK HIGH $92.67, GDXJ JUMPS 9% — Largest Single-Day Gains In Months As $4,200 Gold Translates To Mining Equity Re-Rating
snippet: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) climbed nearly 8% on August 5, 2026, reaching $92.67 — its highest level in over a year — while the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) surged more than 9% to $123.50, both logging their largest single-day percentage gains in months. The moves were driven by a combination of a retreating US dollar, the Iran-Oman Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor agreement, and institutional inflows into hard-asset exposure as September Fed rate-hike probability dropped below 50% for the first time in 2026. GDX's 52-week gain now exceeds 72% and GDXJ's approaches 80%. For retail junior mining investors, the ETF moves signal that institutional capital is flowing into the broader gold equity complex — a precursor that historically drives increased M&A attention and capital market access for junior developers, which have traded at 0.2-0.4x NAV at gold prices that were already materially below today's $4,200+ spot level.

headline: ERO COPPER Q2 2026: REVENUE +74% TO $284M, XAVANTINA GOLD +170% QoQ — Stock Falls As Market Prices In Higher Expectations At $6.22/lb Realized Cu
snippet: Ero Copper Corp. (TSX: ERO) reported Q2 2026 results on August 5 after market close with consolidated copper production of 17,315 tonnes at C1 cash costs of US$2.42 per pound and a realized copper price of US$6.22/lb — generating revenue of US$284.3 million (+73.88% year-on-year) and operating profit of US$107.8 million (+124.79% YoY). The standout operational result was Xavantina gold, which produced 20,553 ounces in Q2 — a 170% quarter-on-quarter increase — materially boosting consolidated margins. Cash from operations was US$137.9 million (+52.75%). Despite the strong results, Ero stock fell on its August 6 earnings call, suggesting the market had priced in even stronger performance at current copper levels. For junior copper developers benchmarking Ero's Caraíba and Xavantina operations as production analogues, Q2's C1 of $2.42/lb underscores the margin environment available to high-grade copper sulphide producers at $6+ copper.

headline: HM EXPLORATION LEWIS PILLEY'S: 18.45m @ 1.14% Cu, 2.42% Zn IN UPPER VMS LENS — Upper Lens Now At 145m Strike, Lower Lens At 40m, Both Open; Phase 2 Fall 2026 (CVE:HM)
snippet: HM Exploration Inc. (CVE: HM) released Phase 1 assay results from holes 8-12 at the Lewis Pilley's Project in Newfoundland's Pilley's Island VMS district on August 4, 2026, with the upper sulphide lens returning 18.45 metres at 1.14% Cu, 2.42% Zn, 16.74 g/t Ag and 0.32 g/t Au — with individual sample high-grade spikes to 8.14% copper and 27.3% zinc — and the lower lens returning 5.42 metres at 1.99% Cu, 1.66% Zn, 15.39 g/t Ag and 0.80 g/t Au, with spikes to 149 g/t silver and 10.23 g/t gold. Both lenses remain open along strike and at depth: the upper lens is now traced over 145 metres of strike and the lower over 40 metres, confirming the volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) geological model that historically produces large tonnage high-grade systems. Phase 2 drilling is scheduled for fall 2026. The Lewis Pilley's intersection pattern is consistent with feeder-zone geometry in VMS systems, where grades and widths typically increase toward the source as drilling advances.

headline: NIOB HITS PEGMATITE IN ALL 8 BARDY HOLES — Rare Earths Confirmed In 6 Of 8; Allanite-Bearing Dykes Over 500m East-West Corridor In Quebec (CSE: NIOB)
snippet: North American Niobium and Critical Minerals Corp. (CSE: NIOB) reported August 4 that its 2026 diamond drill program at the Bardy property in Quebec's Grenville Province achieved a 100% hit rate for the target pegmatite dyke swarm across all 8 holes, with rare-earth-bearing minerals — principally allanite, with parisite in hole BBY-2026-001 and apatite/possible monazite locally — confirmed in 6 of 8 holes across a 500-metre east-west area. Best intersection: hole BBY-2026-006 cut 8.0 metres of syenitic pegmatite from 139.70 to 147.70 metres, terminating in mineralised rock at depth. Assays are submitted to SGS Canada in Val-d'Or. Allanite is a rare-earth-bearing silicate mineral typically associated with neodymium and praseodymium — the magnets-critical elements driving Western rare earth supply chain anxiety — but visual identification alone cannot confirm economic grades; the assay results expected in coming weeks will be the key inflection point for this program.

headline: POWER METALLIC NISK MRE PUSHED TO END-AUGUST — Engineering Firm Capacity Backlog Delays Nisk + Lion Combined Resource Estimate; 5 Rigs Still Drilling (TSX-V: PNPN)
snippet: Power Metallic Mines Inc. (TSX-V: PNPN) announced that the release of its anticipated 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate for the combined Nisk and Lion discoveries at its polymetallic Nisk project in Quebec has been delayed until the end of August due to scheduling constraints at the consulting engineering firm preparing the report — which has the data from Power Metallic but faces concurrent workload conflicts across multiple project assignments. The company maintains 5 rigs actively exploring on the project and confirmed that assay results from the ongoing summer drill program will begin arriving in September and continue through fall 2026. For investors tracking PNPN's upcoming MRE as a near-term catalyst, the delay is logistical rather than geological: Power Metallic continues advancing the program and the resource estimate scope remains unchanged. The Nisk-Lion system has produced polymetallic intersections across nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group elements.

headline: BLUE JAY GOLD STELLER PROJECT: TWO RIGS ADVANCING MT. SKUKUM EPITHERMAL AND SKUKUM CREEK STRUCTURAL TARGETS IN YUKON (TSX-V: JAY)
snippet: Blue Jay Gold Corp. (TSX-V: JAY) provided a Phase 1 drilling update August 6 on the Steller Gold Project in southern Yukon, where two rigs are advancing simultaneously: one testing the Mt. Skukum Epithermal Corridor — the location of the property's only past-producing mine and the highest-priority epithermal target — and the other following structural extensions at the Skukum Creek Au-Ag deposit. The program is supported by the company's contracted LithologIQ system for real-time spectral core logging, enabling same-day geological interpretation of each drill run. Mt. Skukum's past production established the presence of high-grade epithermal gold-silver in the system; the 2026 program is focused on the structural architecture controlling grade distribution, with initial results expected as drilling advances toward targets at each site.

headline: LARGEST US TUNGSTEN DEPOSIT: 1.78MT AT NEVADA BUT NASA BLOCKS A THIRD — $152B Estimate Stuck As China Controls 80% Of Supply, Prices Up 600% Since 2025
snippet: Mining.com reported August 4 that critical minerals developer 3 Proton Lithium (3PL) has identified an inferred tungsten resource of 1.78 million tonnes at its Railroad Valley Minerals project in Nevada — more than five times larger than the next biggest known US deposit — but NASA is blocking development of roughly one-third of the company's claims, citing the flat Nevada terrain's function as a critical satellite instrument calibration site. 3PL estimates the in-situ value at approximately US$152 billion at current prices, which have surged nearly 600% since early 2025 following China's tungsten export controls. Tungsten is essential for armour-piercing munitions (hardened steel penetrators), tooling in aerospace manufacturing, and carbide drill bits — all on the US critical materials priority list. The blocked NASA zone has not been included in the current resource estimate, and production remains at least five years away even in a best-case regulatory scenario. 3PL is lobbying to reverse the land withdrawal, arguing it was imposed in 2023 before the full resource extent was known.

headline: MINERALS 260 AT DIGGERS & DEALERS: BULLABULLING HITS $2.3B POST-TAX NPV, 43% IRR, 2.5 MOZ MAIDEN RESERVE — High-Grade Depth Extensions Drilled (ASX: MI6)
snippet: Minerals 260 Ltd. (ASX: MI6) presented at the Diggers & Dealers Mining Forum in Kalgoorlie (August 3-5, 2026), revealing that the Bullabulling Gold Project's resource has grown from 2.3 million ounces at acquisition in April 2025 to 6.2 million ounces today — a 170% expansion driven by 172,610 metres of drilling with 10 rigs on site — while a maiden ore reserve of 2.5 million ounces and a Pre-Feasibility Study showing a US$2.3 billion post-tax NPV and 43% IRR have now been published. The PFS economics incorporate current gold prices and show a high-margin open-cut development case in Western Australia's established Goldfields mining province. The company has commenced early construction activities including village development, water bore drilling, and grade control drilling. At $4,200 gold, Bullabulling's PFS economics are materially stronger than any prior evaluation of the asset, and MI6's rapid resource expansion trajectory from 2.3 to 6.2 Moz in 15 months of drilling is among the fastest in recent Australian gold development history.
